messages:
ada: heads-up, ran the perf sweep on speculative decoding + draft-model pairing. seeing a weird acceptance-rate cliff when pairing Mixtral drafts with Qwen primary. attaching short log below.

matt: can you paste the log here? quick guess: tokenizer mismatch or kv cache incompatibility.

ada: pasted —
```
[1771234567] request id=xx12 draft= mixtral-7b-draft primary=qwen-7b
  tokens_sent=32 draft_accepts=8 draft_rejects=24 acceptance_rate=0.25
  latency_p50=38ms p95=210ms tail_spikes=3
  note: kv_hit_ratio dropped from 0.92 -> 0.4 after first draft switch
```

sophia: oh that kv_hit_ratio drop is telling. if tokenizer encodings differ we miss prefix matches and cache becomes useless.

julien: also check RoPE scaling mismatch — if the draft uses different RoPE scaling the cached KV from primary won't align for position embeddings, causing scraps in the attention path.

ada: @julien good point — these drafts are same family-ish but Mixtral uses nonstandard RoPE scaling and we don't normalize on decode path for pairing.

perf-bot: perf snapshot: seq_len=64, batch=16, kernel_selection=auto
  baseline(qwen-only): p50=32ms p95=120ms cost_unit=1.0
  pairing(mixtral draft): p50=41ms p95=230ms cost_unit=1.45
  regression_detected: true

matt: action items: (1) confirm tokenizer byte-level compatibility, (2) invalidate/segregate KV cache when pairing across RoPE/kv-dim families, (3) tune acceptance_rate threshold.

kai: for (3) what's current threshold? I recall default was 0.5 for draft acceptance.

ada: current pairing config: ```pairing:{draft_model:"mixtral-7b-draft", acceptance_rate:0.5, fallback:"primary"}``` we observed quality drop even when accepted. broken acceptance -> wasted tokens.

sophia: suggest lowering acceptance target for cross-family pairs to 0.2 and enabling a tokenizer-normalize step: map bytes -> unicode NFKC and then BPE split. That should increase prefix matches and KV hits.

julien: also propose kernel selection hinting: when we know draft/primary have different RoPE scaling, choose kernels that avoid KV reuse and favor fast recompute path (cheaper per-token but avoids cache invalidation overhead). i can add a heuristic: if kv_hit_ratio < 0.6 after 3 tokens, switch to no-cache mode for remaining tokens in that request.

matt: that heuristic sounds reasonable. we should simulate cost: keep a rollout flag to measure unit cost & latency. small AB test 10k requests.

ada: quick config I pushed to staging: ```
pairing_overrides:
  - pair: [qwen-7b, mixtral-7b-draft]
    acceptance_floor: 0.2
    tokenizer_normalize: true
    kv_fallback_policy: segregate
    cache_switch_threshold: 3
    kernel_hint: prefer_recompute_on_mismatch
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for staging/pairing-overrides @ada (id: deploy-20260318-22) :rocket:

perf-bot: preliminary after rollout (2k reqs): acceptance_rate=0.27 kv_hit_ratio=0.78 p50=36ms p95=140ms cost_unit=1.12

kai: that's promising — p95 dropped a lot and cost delta is acceptable. any signs of generation quality regressions?

ada: manual QA: a few edge cases where the draft produced hallucinated completions post-accept; lowering acceptance floor caught most of those. will run eval set overnight.

matt: next steps: (A) keep staging for 48h, (B) instrument per-token KV hit telemetry by model-family and RoPE-id, (C) add a tokenizer-compatibility matrix to model catalog so pairing logic can consult it before enabling caching.

sophia: adding note: we should avoid automatic pairing for models with different kv_dim or head layout until we have robust normalize/fallback. for now keep pairing opt-in for those families.

ada: thanks all. I'll file a small RFC for the tokenizer matrix and an infra ticket for KV telemetry. cc @julien for kernel hints. :thumbsup:
